# Win/loss debrief - the pursuit-side feedback loop

Delivery estimates get honest through the closeout actuals write-back (calibration.md); **pursuit judgment gets honest the same way - through a debrief on every outcome, won AND lost**. Wins teach as much as losses (what actually swung it vs what we assume swung it), and a won/lost log with archetype tags is the only way to know hit-rate by deal type instead of by anecdote. 20 minutes per pursuit, within two weeks of the decision, while the buyer will still talk.

## The 10-question debrief

Ask the decision-maker where possible (a lost buyer is often surprisingly candid); fall back to the champion/coach. Internal-only reconstruction is a last resort - label it as such.

1. **Stated reason** for the decision, in the decision-maker's own words (verbatim if you can get it - this row feeds everything else).
2. **Price vs the winner** - were we higher/lower, and by roughly how much? Was price the reason or the excuse?
3. **Which assumptions or exclusions drew pushback** - the SOW's protective wall (sow-handoff.md) read as scope-dodging, or as rigor?
4. **Timeline credibility** - did our proposed timeline read as realistic, too slow, or suspiciously fast?
5. **Competitor identity** - who won / who else was in it (ISV product, another SI, internal build, do-nothing)?
6. What did the winner show or say that we didn't?
7. Which proposal element landed best (methodology depth, mockups, standard inclusions, references)? Which fell flat?
8. Did they believe the value case / ROI framing - and did it match how they justified the spend internally?
9. Who actually made the call, and was that who we were selling to?
10. Would they include us in the next pursuit - and what would we need to show differently?

## Routing the findings - a debrief that isn't routed is a chat

| Signal | Route to |
|---|---|
| Pricing signals (price vs winner, value-case credibility, floor pressure) | calibration.md notes + bow-pricing-and-value.md doctrine review - as notes, never silent floor changes |
| Proposal patterns (what landed/fell flat, timeline credibility, assumption pushback) | proposal-content.md - update the pattern, not just this pursuit |
| Competitor facts (identity, claims made, pricing heard) | **bow-sales-enablement** battlecard inputs - **sourced + dated per its claims governance** (references/claims-register.md: competitor-sourced facts are never-external; a debrief quote is a source, log who said it and when) |
| Qualification misses (wrong buyer, unwinnable shape, missing prerequisite) | sow-handoff.md qualification checklist |
| Positioning gaps (lost to an ISV we should have conceded, or beat one and don't know why) | proposal-content.md's competitive-positioning section |

## The won/lost log

One row per pursuit outcome, kept alongside the calibration table:

| Pursuit | Date | Won/Lost | Archetype(s) (calibration.md tags) | Deal size | Competitor | Stated reason | Price vs winner | Top lesson + where routed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Review the log when qualifying a new pursuit (step 1 of the SKILL.md workflow): **hit-rate by archetype and by competitor is a qualification input** - a deal shape we lose 4-of-5 times needs a different approach or a polite pass, and knowing which competitor is in the room changes the proposal before it's written.

## Boundaries

- **Delivery actuals** (hours, phases) -> calibration.md via the wd-post-go-live closeout - this reference owns *pursuit* outcomes only.
- **Competitor battlecards and claims governance** -> **bow-sales-enablement**; this reference feeds facts in, never maintains its own competitor file.
- **Client-relationship growth on won-and-delivered work** (QBR, renewal) -> **wd-post-go-live** references/account-growth.md.
